message.reasoning:
I need to decide whether to bid on SHORT_LINE in the auction.

I'll bid $5 to win SHORT_LINE, then mortgage it for $100 before rolling. I need to keep raising to $99 and drop at $100 or above. Cash is tight because of Park Place and Boardwalk.

Short Line would rent for only $25 if unmortgaged, since my other railroads are mortgaged and don't count toward the rent multiplier.

Unmortgage costs $110. A $5 win nets $95 after mortgaging. p2 likely wants Short Line because their B&O is mortgaged.

I'll bid $5 now. Incremental bidding is safer than overpaying to end the auction early. Even if p2 raises to $99, I still profit from mortgaging the property for $100.

I'll bid $5 now. Dropping early would lose the free liquidity from mortgaging SHORT_LINE for $100. After winning, I'll mortgage it before rolling. Cash plus other liquid assets reaches roughly $1091.

Mortgaging SHORT_LINE for $100 still leaves a $4 gap against the $1100 Park Place rent. The current non-LB liquid assets total $996, so winning Short Line under $100 would only reach roughly $1096.

I'm checking whether any other assets can close the remaining $4 gap. Selling the 10 houses on Oriental, Vermont, and Connecticut yields $250. States Avenue is in the pink group with a mortgage value of $70.

Mortgaging the light blue deeds adds $160 in cash, bringing total liquidity to $1156. This covers the $1100 Park Place rent with roughly $56 remaining. Boardwalk at $1400 is still fatal.

A $100 bid would break even in cash but leave me owning a worthless mortgaged railroad. p2 has only $225, so bidding up to $99 also drains their funds and prevents them from building dark blue houses.

p2 has $225 and three houses on each dark blue property. One more house costs $200. I can force them to spend auction cash instead of building. They have already mortgaged most properties, so they cannot mortgage again for cash.

p2 can mortgage Baltic, Kentucky, and Illinois for $260. Combined with their $225 cash, they have $485 total. That is enough to build a dark blue house even after paying the auction bid. Forcing them to spend auction money will not prevent them from upgrading.

The $95 liquidity gain is worth the risk. It lets me mortgage fewer light blues on the next Park hit and preserve more monopoly income. I also need to check whether the auction occurs during my turn or p2's, since paying $5 immediately would reduce cash before I can mortgage.

The auction is on p2's turn. I will mortgage SHORT_LINE before rolling on my turn. p2 could still build a fourth house on Park Place during their turn, since they have $225 and the auction bid is only about $5.

A fourth house on Park Place would raise rent to $1300. Even with the extra $100 from Short Line, total liquidity remains roughly $1256, which still cannot survive that hit. If p2 builds, Short Line does not prevent the loss. The real value is preserving more of the light blue monopoly when they do not build. I am also considering bidding higher to drain p2's cash below $200 so they cannot afford a fourth house this turn.
